note: Lab 4 (2026-11-07): why shots morph. A first frame only + camera prompt, B first+last with a SMALL move in the same scene, C first+last with a BIG move (the method that scored 2-4 in production), D first frame only with an orbit. Rerun: first run's results failed to push. All 4 scored 3.0, which smells like a miscalibrated reviewer, so keep the review issues and judge by eye too.
image_rules: No watermark, no border, no logos, no text, no stick figures. Vertical 9:16 composition for a phone screen.

A cardboard computer-tower villain lair on a workbench. Centre: a cardboard machine with a big lever on its side and one glowing red LED eye. It stands next to the lever, reaching for it. Wide shot, camera at penguin eye height. Calm lower fifth.

Keep every object, colour and proportion identical. motion_tests.prompt: Slow, steady push-in toward the penguin. The penguin grabs the lever with both flippers and pulls it down; the machine's red LED eye glows brighter. One continuous shot. Every object keeps its shape, size and position. Stop-motion miniature feel, no morphing, no new objects.
The camera eases a little closer and lower as the penguin pulls the lever down; the red LED eye glows brighter. One continuous shot, nothing morphs.
The camera cranes up and over to a top-down view of the workbench as the penguin pulls the lever. One continuous shot, nothing morphs.

The camera orbits 60 degrees around the cardboard machine while the penguin pulls the lever; the red LED eye flares. One continuous shot. Every object keeps its shape, size and position. Stop-motion miniature feel, no morphing, no new objects.
